---
title: "PPSV Project Management System"
---

This protocol documents the management system for the Protein Production
and Structural Validation Facility (PPSV) at the Max Planck Institute of
Biochemistry.

The production application exists at
`https://ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/ppsv-app/`. For facility questions, contact
[ppsv-request@biochem.mpg.de](mailto:ppsv-request@biochem.mpg.de) or
+49 89 8578-3629. for help with the system contact [omicsdesk@biochem.mpg.de](mailto:omicsdesk@biochem.mpg.de)

## Scope

The system supports eight PPSV service modules plus a separate general-inquiry
path. Every saved project receives a unique Id, such as `PPSV000001`, `PPSV000002`, and so on. 
Its lifecycle uses these seven statuses:

1. `Submitted`
2. `Under review`
3. `Accepted`
4. `In progress`
5. `Awaiting requester input`
6. `Completed`
7. `Closed`

The application records the current status, owner, assignee, contact snapshot,
status history, file manifest, archive state, ticket state, and every mail
attempt. A PPSV-branded PDF summarizes the request without any cost or invoice
data.

General inquiries are stored as `request_kind = inquiry`; they are not a ninth
service-module database row. Service requests use the fields in
`PPSV_Submission_form.xlsx` exactly as described in the
[field dictionary](chapters/field-dictionary.qmd).

## Trust model

Apache authenticates the user with LDAP and injects server-controlled profile
headers after removing client-supplied versions. Shiny Server listens only on
`127.0.0.1:3838`. Roles are derived case-insensitively from a version-controlled
allowlist, and every repository or server action repeats its authorization
check. UI visibility is never treated as a security boundary.

Files are not served from the application directory. They are stored under the
facility pool or a persistent fallback, use generated stored names, and are
verified by checksum before download or reconciliation.

## Deliberate exclusions

PPSV v1 does not contain:

- legacy MS project data or a migration from `ms_projects.db`;
- MS-specific forms, sample tables, templates, or data-release workflows;
- price lists, costs, cost estimates, billing calculations, or invoices;
- inbound-mail forwarding or a mailbox relay;
- production local-password login or identity in a query string/cookie; or
- permanent deletion of requests or files.
